items.text: Visited the Hall of Maritime History last weekend and was pleasantly surprised by how well the new audio guide works. The app uses an AI assistant to answer questions about the exhibits, and it correctly identified the 18th-century sextant when I pointed my phone at it. My only complaint is that the system occasionally repeated the same paragraph twice, which felt like a glitch. Still, for a free tool it added a lot to the visit, and I'd recommend it to anyone going with kids.

items.text: Heads up for anyone still on v2 of the Northwind API: the deprecation is scheduled for March 31, and the migration guide at northwind.example/docs/migrate-v3 is actually useful. I ran the automated tool they provide and it flagged two endpoints we'd forgotten about, which saved us a lot of guesswork. The only annoyance is that the tool's AI assistant kept suggesting the same fix for a pagination issue, but a quick manual edit sorted it out. If you haven't started, do it now rather than the week before the cutoff.

items.text:
I've been going to the Riverside Community Clinic for years, and the recent switch to an AI assistant for scheduling has been a mixed bag. On the one hand, it's easy to get a same-day slot for a nurse visit; on the other, the assistant sometimes misunderstands what kind of appointment you need.

Last month I asked for a follow-up with Dr. Okafor and the system booked me with a different physician entirely. When I called to fix it, the receptionist was apologetic and said the tool is still learning. I appreciate the transparency, but I'd rather have the option to skip the assistant and talk to a person.

If you do use it, double-check the confirmation screen before you hit submit. And if you need anything complex, just call the front desk—they're faster anyway.

items.text: Just got back from the Museum of Modern Craft and their new chatbot guide is genuinely helpful for finding exhibits by medium. I asked it for ceramics and it gave me a short tour route that included the basement kiln room, which I'd have missed otherwise. It occasionally mispronounced artist names, but the system is clearly a work in progress. Worth trying if you're overwhelmed by the floor plan.
